newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK urged to cut red tape on property development.
newsitem.headline: HK urged to cut red tape on property development.

text.p: Hong Kong's business lobby urged the government on Tuesday to cut bureaucratic procedures to speed up property development projects in the territory.
The Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce said in a statement it had given Chief Secretary Anson Chan a position paper calling on her to cut red tape.

"In view of the ever rising demand for residential and commerical property, we consider that the public interest would be better served by streamlining the property development process," the Chamber's director Ian Christie said.
The chamber said the process of building private housing flats -- from identification of strategic sites to completion -- took 11 to 14 years.
"Much time and cost could be saved if a statutory time limit is imposed for all procedures and if some procedures are conducted concurrently, rather than consecutively," Christie said.
